Read CME Globex instrument definitions

Source: R/cme.R
cme_definitions.Rd

Reads instrument definitions in Databento's definition schema for the CME Globex dataset (GLBX.MDP3) and keeps one row per instrument phase: the period during which an instrument identifier denotes one contract. Every column is coerced by content, not by its stored type, so files in which all columns arrived as text (which happens when one column holds an unexpected value) read the same as typed files.

Usage

cme_definitions(x, classes = c("C", "P", "F"))

Arguments

x

A data.frame of definition records, or path(s) to Parquet (needs the arrow package) or CSV files, or directories containing them.

classes

Instrument classes to keep: "C" call, "P" put, "F" future (default). Spreads ("S", "T", "M") are dropped unless listed.

Value

A tibble of class cme_definitions, one row per instrument phase, with columns instrument_id, valid_from, valid_to (POSIXct, UTC), deleted (logical: the phase ended with a deletion record), ts_recv (receive time of the phase's most recent record), raw_symbol, asset (product code, e.g. "6M"), instrument_class, type ("call", "put", "future", or NA), exercise ("american", "european", or NA), cfi, expiration (POSIXct, UTC), strike, underlying_id, underlying, currency, unit_of_measure.

Details

Reused identifiers. The exchange assigns an expired or deleted contract's instrument_id to a new contract, sometimes within days and across classes (a call can become a put, a spread an option). A phase is a run of records for one identifier with the same raw_symbol (or, without symbols, the same class, strike, and expiration date), in receive-time order. A modification that only changes, say, the expiration time stays in the same phase; a deletion record (security_update_action = "D") ends it. Each phase reports the attributes of its most recent record and is valid from its first record (valid_from) until the next phase of the same identifier starts or the deletion arrives (valid_to; NA while open). cme_option_surfaces() assigns each daily statistic to the phase in force on its trading date.

Exercise style. For options, the third character of the ISO 10962 CFI code is the exercise style (A American, E European). On CME currency options it differs across products and years — for example, weekly and monthly contracts on the same future can differ — so it is read per instrument rather than assumed.

Expiration. expiration is the last eligible trade time (UTC) as published by the exchange. Expiry times differ across products and years, so use this field rather than a fixed clock time.

References

Databento documentation of the instrument-definition schema and of the CME Globex MDP 3.0 dataset (GLBX.MDP3), https://databento.com/docs/venues-and-datasets/glbx-mdp3.

See also

cme_statistics(), cme_option_surfaces().

Examples

defs <- data.frame(
  ts_recv = c("2016-06-01T00:00:00Z", "2016-06-02T00:00:00Z", "2016-06-01T00:00:00Z"),
  instrument_id = c("11", "11", "20"),
  raw_symbol = c("6BN6 C1450", "6BN6 C1450", "6BN6"),
  asset = c("6B", "6B", "6B"),
  instrument_class = c("C", "C", "F"),
  cfi = c("OCAFPS", "OCAFPS", "FFCXSX"),
  expiration = c("2016-07-08T19:00:00Z", "2016-07-08T19:00:00Z", "2016-09-19T14:16:00Z"),
  strike_price = c("1.45", "1.45", ""),
  underlying_id = c("20", "20", "0")
)
cme_definitions(defs)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 17
#>   instrument_id valid_from          valid_to deleted
#>           <dbl> <dttm>              <dttm>   <lgl>  
#> 1            11 2016-06-01 00:00:00 NA       FALSE  
#> 2            20 2016-06-01 00:00:00 NA       FALSE  
#> # ℹ 13 more variables: ts_recv <dttm>, raw_symbol <chr>, asset <chr>,
#> #   instrument_class <chr>, type <chr>, exercise <chr>, cfi <chr>,
#> #   expiration <dttm>, strike <dbl>, underlying_id <dbl>, underlying <chr>,
#> #   currency <chr>, unit_of_measure <chr>
